set.description: Bohemia Interactive's 2001 military sandbox returns with a modern, open-source Poseidon engine, native 64-bit Windows and Linux builds, full gamepad controls, in-game mods and a rebuilt multiplayer browser. The engine source is public; the full campaigns and data remain part of a commercial game purchase.

systemRequirements.min: Windows 10/11 x64 or Linux x64 with glibc 2.31+; dual-core 2.0 GHz CPU; 4 GB RAM; OpenGL 3.3-capable GPU with 512 MB VRAM; OpenAL audio; 20 GB free. Linux needs Mesa 20+ or a suitable proprietary driver (official Steam listing).
systemRequirements.recommended: Windows 10/11 x64 or Linux x64 with glibc 2.31+; quad-core 3.0 GHz CPU; 8 GB RAM; OpenGL 4.x GPU with at least 1 GB VRAM; OpenAL audio; 20 GB free (official Steam listing).

min.notes: Windows 10/11 or Linux glibc 2.31+; Mesa 20+ or suitable graphics driver on Linux. OpenAL-compatible audio.

recommended.notes: Windows 10/11 or Linux glibc 2.31+; current graphics driver and OpenAL audio.

set.launcherInstall.note: The commercial full game is available through GOG on Windows and Steam on Windows/Linux. The engine source is GPL-3.0-or-later but the campaigns and data are not an unrestricted free download. PlayBound does not bundle those assets or currently provision its PoseidonServer on the VPS. After purchase/install, executable pickup and full gamepad/party flow need a live test. Do not confuse the remaster with the older macOS/Linux port of classic CWA.

qualityBar.verdict: It still makes crossing an empty field feel like a serious tactical decision, now without fighting the display settings first.

set.longDescription:
Arma: Cold War Assault Remastered keeps the nervous scale of Bohemia Interactive's first military sandbox. An infantry patrol can begin as a quiet map-reading exercise and end with everybody trying to remember where the last shot came from. Vehicles extend the distance between safety and disaster, while the mission editor lets players construct situations that the campaign never planned. The game asks you to pay attention to ground, cover and timing. Sprinting at the objective may work once. Making a plan that survives contact with a hillside is the more satisfying skill.

The 2026 remaster modernizes the original Poseidon engine without turning the underlying game into a different kind of shooter. Bohemia lists native 64-bit builds for Windows and Linux, ultrawide and high-refresh support, a new OpenGL 3.3 renderer, modern audio, and full gamepad controls with rebinding and response tuning. The new multiplayer backend has a master server and in-game browser in place of the old GameSpy dependency. There is also an in-game mod manager and an open toolchain for players who enjoy changing missions or making new material. The engine and game source are available under GPL-3.0-or-later. The campaign data and assets follow a separate Bohemia license and remain tied to the commercial release. Public source code does not make a purchased campaign free to redistribute.

There is plenty for a group to do. The remaster supports online and LAN multiplayer, including competitive and cooperative missions. The official CWR source includes a PoseidonServer target, and a server guide describes Windows and Linux executables included with a normal game installation. It can load a configuration file, announce itself to the modern browser, accept direct IP joins and rotate missions. That is a real dedicated-server path, but PlayBound has not installed licensed game data on its VPS or built a tested hosting recipe. Parties can coordinate a session and send players toward the game's own browser; automatic join handoff and PlayBound-hosted servers are still unverified. A numerical player cap is not established by the store listing, so this Draft does not pretend a sample server configuration is the maximum.

The existing PlayBound store link points to GOG's Windows purchase. Steam lists the remaster for Windows and Linux; Linux players should use that supported release rather than assume the GOG download contains a Linux binary. The official minimum is Windows 10/11 or Linux with glibc 2.31+, a dual-core 2 GHz x64 CPU, 4 GB RAM, OpenGL 3.3 graphics with 512 MB VRAM and 20 GB free. Recommended memory is 8 GB with a quad-core CPU and OpenGL 4.x graphics. Cover, screenshots and video remain from the existing game record and their links currently respond.

This listing stays Draft while we test store install detection, a full controller session and multiplayer joining on the current remaster. The value is not a nostalgic menu of old missions alone. It is the feeling that one road, one tree line and one badly timed vehicle movement can turn a simple operation into a story everyone in the squad remembers differently.
set.whyWePickedIt: A genuine classic with modern Windows/Linux builds, full native controller support, a usable multiplayer browser and open engine source. The commercial game assets and PlayBound hosting path still need to be handled with the same care as the technical improvements.
set.thatOneThing: An empty field can be the most frightening thing on the map once your squad has to cross it under observation.

installSteps.text: Buy and install the full remaster from GOG or Steam. The open-source engine alone does not include the purchased campaigns and game data. PlayBound's GOG link opens the official Windows listing.
Use the official Steam remaster for the native Linux x64 build. The GOG offer shown on this record is for Windows; do not assume it supplies Linux files.
Launch once through your store client and configure display and controller bindings. PlayBound's automatic detection of the remastered executable has not yet been verified; use Locate if needed.

firstPlaySteps.text: Run a short mission to tune the native gamepad deadzone and response, then check the in-game mod manager before joining a modified server.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: Use Multiplayer in the remastered client to browse Internet or LAN servers, or connect by direct address. Match the server's mission and required mods. A PlayBound party can coordinate players; automatic lobby handoff has not been verified.
The remaster includes a PoseidonServer dedicated target, but PlayBound has not provisioned the required commercial game files or validated a VPS recipe for it.

faq.q: Is the remaster free because the engine is open source?
faq.a: No. Bohemia released the engine and game source, while the full campaigns and game assets remain a commercial purchase. A separate Steam demo can test the engine.

faq.q: Does it work with a controller?
faq.a: Yes. Bohemia lists full native gamepad support with rebindable controls and response tuning. PlayBound has not yet tested an end-to-end controller session.

faq.q: Which platforms have a supported remaster?
faq.a: The current official remaster lists Windows and Linux x64. The existing GOG offer is Windows; Steam lists both Windows and Linux.

faq.q: Can PlayBound host its dedicated server?
faq.a: The game includes a dedicated server executable, but PlayBound has not provisioned licensed game data on the VPS or verified a hosting recipe.

bestFor: Squads that enjoy deliberate, mission-based combat
Players who want classic missions with modern displays and native gamepad support
notFor: Players expecting a free full campaign from the source-code release
Players seeking an already-tested PlayBound dedicated server

expected.description: MechWarrior: Living Legends (MWLL) is a standalone freeware multiplayer action simulation built on CryEngine, putting players in control of iconic BattleMechs, Battle Armor, hovercraft, tanks, and aerospace fighters across massive combined-arms battlefields.

installSteps.text: Install the PlayBound Launcher, then find MechWarrior: Living Legends and press Install. The launcher downloads the official release, unpacks it and creates a shortcut. This is the fastest route and it never uses third-party mirrors.

Alternatively, download MechWarrior: Living Legends directly from the official site at https://mechlivinglegends.net/. Always download from the official source — third-party mirrors of free games are a common malware vector.

Run the downloaded installer and follow the prompts. If Windows SmartScreen warns about an unrecognised publisher, that is normal for open-source projects without a paid code-signing certificate — choose More info, then Run anyway.
Launch the game and look at the settings menu before your first session — resolution and control defaults are worth checking. MechWarrior: Living Legends needs roughly 8.0 GB of free disk space.

set.description: A free, standalone BattleTech combined-arms game built on Crysis Wars. Pilot BattleMechs, tanks, aircraft, hovercraft and battle armor on large online maps. The official Windows installer first installs MWLL's own launcher, which then downloads the full game; PlayBound does not yet automate that second stage.
set.developerName: MechWarrior: Living Legends community development team

systemRequirements.min: Windows; x64-capable Intel Core 2 2.0 GHz or AMD Athlon 64; 4 GB RAM; GeForce 7800 or Radeon 2900 Pro with 512 MB VRAM; DirectX 9.0c/10; allow 10–15 GB plus future maps (official MWLL wiki).
systemRequirements.recommended: Windows 7 or later per the official guide; Intel Core i3 9000-series 3.7 GHz+ or Ryzen 3000-series or newer; at least 4 GB RAM; GeForce GTX 1060 or Radeon RX 470 with 4 GB VRAM for 1080p; DirectX 9.0c/10; 10–15 GB plus maps. Windows 10/11 are more practical current targets.

min.cpuText: Intel Core 2 2.0 GHz or AMD Athlon 64
min.gpuText: NVIDIA GeForce 7800 or ATI Radeon 2900 Pro
min.notes: The official wiki lists older Windows versions for the CryEngine base. Allow more disk for downloaded maps and use a current supported Windows release.

recommended.cpuText: Intel Core i3 9000-series 3.7 GHz+ or AMD Ryzen 3000-series or newer
recommended.gpuText: NVIDIA GTX 1060 or AMD RX 470 for 1080p
recommended.notes: The official guide emphasizes single-thread CPU speed. Maps add disk use; the guide does not raise the recommended RAM above 4 GB.

set.launcherInstall.note: The official 72 MB MWLL-Installer.exe installs the MWLL Launcher, which downloads and updates the full game on first run. Treating that bootstrap EXE as a completed direct-installer would falsely mark a partial install as playable. PlayBound links to the official process until it can follow and verify the second stage. The developer says Crysis Wars ownership is not required. Dedicated servers are configured through the MWLL Launcher but PlayBound has no VPS recipe. XInput/joystick support is incomplete: the official troubleshooting guide says torso/turret twist still needs keyboard or mouse.

qualityBar.verdict: The scale is the draw: giant machines matter, but the battle belongs to whoever understands the whole combined-arms map.

set.longDescription:
MechWarrior: Living Legends makes the battlefield feel larger than the cockpit you first enter. A BattleMech can dominate a road, but a tank may hold the angle you ignored and an aircraft may arrive while everyone is watching the duel. Battle armor and hovercraft add more ways to get close, scout and exploit a gap. The game is a BattleTech combined-arms conversion built on Crysis Wars, now distributed as a free standalone setup. The community team says you do not need to buy Crysis Wars separately. That makes its scale more interesting: friends can meet on the same battlefield without comparing old boxed-game keys first.

The variety of vehicles changes how a match is read. Heavy armor is impressive but not an answer to every problem; pilots need to think about range, terrain, repair, air cover and which asset is worth risking for an objective. A fast aircraft and a slow ground unit can contribute to the same push in very different ways. The official site describes a current community-built game with a roster of more than seventy units, while its wiki documents maps, controls and server configuration. This is not a single-player campaign wearing a multiplayer badge. The online battlefield and the people who fill it are the point.

The official Windows download begins with a roughly 72 MB installer. That installer sets up MWLL's own launcher; on first run, the launcher pulls the complete game and Crysis Wars demo components, then updates them. The small download is therefore only a bootstrap, not the installed game. PlayBound currently sends players to the official download page. Our generic direct-installer flow would otherwise mark the launcher as a finished install before its content update was complete. That needs a dedicated, tested two-stage recipe before we can promise one-click installation. The full install asks for roughly 10–15 GB, with more space for additional maps.

MWLL has online servers and an official dedicated-server configuration path in its launcher. The configuration UI covers map rotation, mode-specific settings, capacity, password, server port and remote management. The guide lists UDP 64100 as its default game port. PlayBound has not provisioned or tested that dedicated server on the VPS, so this Draft should not appear as ready for one-click hosting. A PlayBound party can coordinate friends around the official server browser; automatic connection to a chosen server still needs a live test. A current, verified absolute player maximum is not documented in the materials we reviewed, so the card leaves it unspecified.

Input needs equal honesty. Crysis Wars understands XInput devices, but the MWLL troubleshooting guide says joystick setup requires an emulator and torso or turret twist with joystick/gamepad remains problematic. We are not marking this as complete controller support or shipping an untested PlayBound Controls profile. Keyboard and mouse are the dependable starting point. The official hardware guidance spans very old minimum parts through modern 1080p recommendations and notes that single-thread CPU speed matters. This record stays Draft while we test a complete install, party handoff, controls and a real hosted server. The reason it deserves that work is the wonderful moment when you realize your large, expensive-looking Mech is only one piece of a much bigger fight.
set.whyWePickedIt: A free standalone combined-arms BattleTech game with real community servers and a documented host configuration path fits PlayBound's multiplayer focus. Its two-stage installer and incomplete gamepad behavior need a game-specific solution before release.
set.thatOneThing: Your BattleMech can win the duel in front of it and still lose the fight to the aircraft nobody bothered to watch.

installSteps.text: Download MWLL-Installer.exe from the official MechWarrior: Living Legends downloads page. The roughly 72 MB file installs MWLL Launcher, not the complete game.

Run the installer to a writable games folder, then open MWLL Launcher and choose Update. Let it download and verify the full game before trying to play. The project says no separate Crysis Wars purchase is required.
Choose a profile name in MWLL Launcher and press Launch. PlayBound's generic installer pickup has not been verified for this two-stage setup; use the official launcher until it is.

firstPlaySteps.text: Start with keyboard and mouse, learn how vehicle classes complement one another, and use the in-game Internet Games browser for a populated server. Gamepad and joystick movement are incomplete according to the official troubleshooting guide.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: Open Multiplayer, then Internet Game in MWLL and select a live server. A PlayBound party can organize friends, but automatic server joining has not been verified.
The official MWLL Launcher can configure a dedicated server, including map rotation and password. PlayBound has not installed or validated a VPS recipe for this game.

faq.q: Do I need to own Crysis Wars?
faq.a: No. The official MWLL site says its installer supplies the legal Crysis Wars components needed to play.

faq.q: Why is the first download only about 72 MB?
faq.a: It installs MWLL Launcher. That launcher downloads the full game and updates it on first run; 10–15 GB of disk space is a better starting allowance.

faq.q: Can I use a controller or flight stick?
faq.a: Crysis Wars accepts XInput, and a community joystick setup guide exists, but the official troubleshooting page says some torso/turret controls still need keyboard or mouse. PlayBound has not verified a full controller profile.

faq.q: Can PlayBound host a dedicated server?
faq.a: MWLL has a documented dedicated-server configuration tool, but PlayBound has not yet deployed and tested it on the VPS.

bestFor: Teams who want BattleTech vehicles in one large online fight
Players who enjoy combined-arms tactics more than a solo campaign
notFor: Players expecting a single-file automatic install today
Players who require complete native gamepad or HOTAS control
